item.title: Women politicians face tech-facilitated violence in Uganda’s 2026 elections
item.description: Ideally, the law that is supposed to protect women online is the Computer Misuse Act 2011, but it has instead been used to attack feminist dissenters.

item.title: Nigeria confronts growing climate risks with rising droughts, heatwaves, and flooding
item.description: In 2022, Nigeria was the third-highest country in internal displacement in Africa, primarily caused by conflict and flood, a climate change induced disaster.

item.title: Impunity and unsolved crimes against journalists kill public trust
item.description: The safety of journalists is no longer just about physical protection, but a complex intersection of legal resilience, digital hygiene, and psychological support.

item.title: Environmental defenders labeled ‘terrorists’ for bringing renewable power to Philippine communities
item.description: Accusing activists of having links to terrorism has led to non-profit funds being frozen and local climate projects being delayed or scrapped.

item.title: Pakistan jails two lawyers for 17 years over old tweets
item.description: Two Pakistani human rights lawyers received 17-year sentences under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) after criticizing military abuses online, raising concerns about due process and free expression.

item.title: After alleged racist insult, an Argentine tourist faces the possibility of prison time in Brazil
item.description: Many people on social media reacted with surprise to the story of the Argentine visitor arrested for allegedly making racial insults. Racism is a non-bailable offense in Brazil.

item.title: Iran’s internet blackout as media event: Networks, algorithms, and the politics of visibility
item.description: As Iran went dark, who could speak — and who couldn’t — reshaped how the world understood a nationwide uprising

item.title: How the series ‘The Eternaut’ revived searches for the disappeared in Argentina
item.description: The family of Héctor Germán Oesterheld, author of the comic strip behind the series, lost nine members to the dictatorship: Oesterheld himself, his four daughters, two sons-in-law and two grandchildren.

item.title: Bosnian-Herzegovinian professor Nejra Turčinović returns to an old passion: silly Illustrations for children
item.description: “We should give children as many illustrations as possible, including new, hand-drawn ones that give them a different perspective on fairy tales or stories [and] might encourage them to draw...”

item.title: Nearly 200 people massacred by gunmen in Kaiama LGA, Nigeria
item.description: Security experts and human rights organizations have linked the cause of the attacks to porous borders, reactive security approach, and spillover of extremist groups.
